01 / The perspective

A temple is more than a building: it is sacred space, made with intention

A temple or spiritual center brings together the land, its orientation, the sanctum, the halls, the entrances and the devotees who gather there. In the Vaastu tradition, the arrangement of these elements is considered in relation to the sacred purpose of the space.

Dr. Ravi Rao provides Vaastu consultations for temples and spiritual spaces, combining traditional spatial principles with the practical requirements of architecture and construction.

03 / Scope of consultation

Every part of the sacred space
has its place

The consultation considers the site as a whole, while addressing the function of each part of the temple or spiritual space.

Site & Surroundings

Land, orientation, approach roads and the surroundings of the proposed temple or sacred space.

Sanctum & DeityGarbhagriha

Placement of the sanctum, the direction the deity faces and the main axis of the temple.

Entrances & Circulation

Main gate, entrances, circumambulation paths and the movement of devotees.

Halls & Gathering SpacesMandapas

Prayer halls, assembly and ceremony spaces, and their relation to the sanctum.

Ritual Spaces & Sacred Elements

Placement of homa or yajna areas, lamps and water, together with supporting utilities.

Existing Temples

Review of existing temples and spiritual centers, with practical recommendations where feasible.

04 / Spaces

Spiritual Spaces We Serve

Specialized spatial guidance for sacred spaces of every kind, from a single shrine to a temple complex.

Temples & Shrines

Sanctum, deity placement, entrances and the layout of the shrine.

Temple Complexes

Shrines, halls, courtyards and the flow of devotees through the complex.

Pavilions & Chhatris

Open pavilions, courtyards and sacred structures within the grounds.

Garden & Home Shrines

Small shrines in gardens and private grounds.

Yajna & Ritual Grounds

Fire-ritual areas, seating and the space around them.

Ceremonial Halls

Halls for rituals, ceremonies and community gatherings.

An important consideration

Begin with the land
and honor it from
the first stone

A temple is built to serve generations. Considering Vaastu at the planning stage allows recommendations to be reviewed alongside architectural and structural plans — before construction makes changes more difficult.

06 / From the Journal

Prana Pratishtha: how a temple is brought to life

Prana Pratishtha is the ritual of consecration in which a deity is invoked into the murti and a temple becomes a living place of worship. The article looks at what the ceremony means, how the site and the sanctum are prepared for it, and where Vaastu fits between the first stone and the first prayer.

07 / Questions

Before you get in touch

Can Vaastu be applied to an existing temple?

Yes. For existing temples the consultation reviews the current arrangement and recommends practical adjustments where feasible.

Does it replace our architect or sthapati?

No. Recommendations are coordinated with architectural and structural requirements and with your project team.

When is the best time to involve Vaastu?

At the planning stage — site selection and layout planning — before construction begins.
